To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel offline window-less algorithm for clustering sensor data that can be used in terrain coverage.
we have developed a windowless clustering algorithm that can be used with different classifiers and that can cluster data for fast switching systems.
we have developed a new windowless algorithm for clustering sensor data from the terrain, which has been successfully tested using both synthetic and real data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel clustering algorithm to automatically identify terrain classes.
the development of algorithms that enable autonomous systems to develop terrain classifiers without any human interaction or feedback.
the problem of clustering sensor data for terrain classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our algorithm can be used to cluster data for any classifier, provided it can output a probability value for a given input.
our algorithm is capable of clustering data from complex systems with high process noise and/or high observation noise, and that it is capable of clustering real data from a mobile robot.
the proposed algorithm has the ability to cluster sensor data for terrain identification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a novel windowless algorithm to cluster sensor data from the terrain, which is suitable for use in autonomous systems.
we developed an offline clustering algorithm for terrain classification, which is able to identify the different terrains, even when the system has high process and/or observation noise.

the algorithm is capable of clustering data from the same type of terrain, even when there is high process and/or observation noise and/or when the data is not normally distributed, and even when the terrain is changing quickly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clustering of time-correlated data can be done using a windowless algorithm.
the windowless approach is more robust than the windowed approach in the face of noise.

the algorithm is capable of identifying the same underlying distribution in data, despite the fact that it is not window-based, and hence does not rely on the duration of time a system spends in a state.
